summary: 5 completed games from 2026-09-14 through 2026-09-20. 26 engine review positions. 40 minutes of source-backed foundational study. Previous 1 archived weeks contained 0 games total; activity comparison only.

review.narrative: Engine review found at least one major evaluation swing in 5 of 5 analyzed games (100%). 2 of 5 timed games (40%) had a strongest cue after a quick decision. Forced-mate swings appeared in 2 of 5 games (40%). The strongest cue occurred in the middlegame in 3 of 5 games (60%). 5 games is a small sample, so treat this as a pattern to inspect, not proof of one weakness. Review the linked positions first, then use the checklist below to practise the decision process those positions call for.

focus.reason: 5 of 5 reviewed games (100%) matched “major evaluation swings.” This exercise is a response to that measured pattern, not a claim about its chess cause.
exercises: Read the introductory candidate-selection prose. At two positions from a completed game, list serious moves for both sides before using analysis. Explain why each move deserves attention.
Identify one omitted candidate or justify why the position has few serious choices.
playReminders: What serious alternative or opposing reply have I left out?

focus.reason: 5 of 5 reviewed games (100%) matched “major evaluation swings.” This exercise is a response to that measured pattern, not a claim about its chess cause.
exercises: Read Blumenfeld’s rule. Revisit three completed-game decisions: select a move, pause, and check immediate mates and hanging material before revealing the continuation. Use a mental reset.
Perform the same brief inspection on all three intended moves, including any changed choice.
playReminders: After my move, is there an immediate mate or a piece hanging?

focus.reason: 2 of 5 reviewed games (40%) matched “rushed critical decisions.” This exercise is a response to that measured pattern, not a claim about its chess cause.
exercises: Read Time-trouble. Review one rapid game’s longest thinks and two rushed decisions. Record which time use answered a concrete question; practise two familiar positions with a short timer.
Name one avoidable source of wasted time and one decision that deserved more attention.
playReminders: Use my own pace; check what changed before continuing.

generalReminders: Before moving, check both sides’ checks, captures and immediate threats.
